findings.title: XSS via unescaped URL interpolation into raw HTML post content
findings.body: TopicEmbed.import builds the 'imported from' footer by interpolating the caller-supplied `url` directly into an HTML anchor: `"#{url}"`. The post is then created with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, which (per Post#cook in app/models/post.rb line 133) returns `raw` verbatim with no sanitization. A URL containing a single quote (e.g. `http://x/' onmouseover='alert(1)`) or HTML like `http://x/'>

findings.title: Raw HTML from remote feeds is stored and rendered without sanitization
findings.body: TopicEmbed.import creates posts with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, and Post#cook (app/models/post.rb line 133) returns `raw` unchanged for that method, bypassing the entire Markdown/sanitization pipeline. The `contents` come from an external RSS/Atom feed (Jobs::PollFeed passes `i.content.scrub` — `scrub` only replaces invalid byte sequences, it does not sanitize HTML) or from `Readability::Document` output in import_remote. Any script, event handler, or iframe in the feed content is stored verbatim in `cooked` and rendered unescaped via `<%= raw post.cooked %>` in app/views/embed/best.html.erb line 19 and in the regular topic view. A compromised or malicious feed source yields stored XSS against every viewer of the imported topic. The content must be passed through Sanitize (as the normal cooking pipeline does) before being stored.

findings.title: Referer host check compares against a single configured host, allowing bypass and enabling unauthorized embedding
findings.body: ensure_embeddable validates only that `URI(request.referer).host == SiteSetting.embeddable_host`. Two problems: (1) the Referer header is fully client-controlled — an attacker can simply send a request with a forged `Referer: http://<embeddable_host>/` header (e.g. via curl) and pass the check, so this is not an authorization boundary at all; (2) the check is an exact string match against one host, so subdomains or any other legitimate embedding host are rejected, and conversely any page on the configured host (including attacker-controlled paths if the host serves user content) is accepted. Combined with the fact that the endpoint renders full topic content (TopicView with posts) for any `embed_url` whose host matches `embeddable_host` (see TopicRetriever#invalid_host?), this exposes forum content to scraping and enables the iframe to be embedded from arbitrary pages on that host. The referer check should be treated as defense-in-depth only; access control must not rely on it.

findings.title: X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL is an invalid value and disables framing protection
findings.body: The controller sets `response.headers['X-Frame-Options'] = "ALLOWALL"`. ALLOWALL is not a valid X-Frame-Options directive (valid values are DENY and SAMEORIGIN, plus the obsolete ALLOW-FROM uri). Browsers ignore unrecognized values, so this header provides no protection and signals intent to allow framing from anywhere. Since the whole point of the referer check is to restrict which sites may frame this content, the header should either be removed (relying on the referer check) or set to a real value; as written it is dead code that gives a false sense of security. Additionally, modern browsers enforce framing via CSP frame-ancestors, which is not set here.

findings.title: postMessage origin check uses indexOf, which is bypassable
findings.body: The message handler validates the sender with `if (discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1) { return; }`. `String#indexOf` performs a substring match, so an origin like `http://evil.com/?x=http://discourse.example.com` (or `http://discourse.example.com.evil.com` if discourseUrl lacks a scheme/trailing slash) contains the discourse URL as a substring and passes the check. A malicious page could then send a `discourse-resize` message with an arbitrary height, resizing the iframe to hide or distort content (a clickjacking/UX-integrity issue; the data is only a height so impact is limited, but the check is still wrong). The origin must be compared exactly: `e.origin !== discourseUrl` (after normalizing both to origins).

findings.title: postMessage targetOrigin is the raw Referer header, enabling message leakage to attacker-controlled origins
findings.body: The layout sends the resize message with `parent.postMessage({...}, '<%= request.referer %>')`. The targetOrigin is taken verbatim from the client-controlled Referer header. If the Referer is not a valid origin (e.g. a full URL with a path, or an attacker-supplied value), the browser behavior is undefined/lenient in older engines, and more importantly the referer is attacker-controlled, so the height data (and the fact that the embed loaded) can be posted to an origin the site operator never intended. targetOrigin should be a fixed, known origin — the configured `SiteSetting.embeddable_host` (normalized to scheme://host) — not the request's Referer. Also note `request.referer` is interpolated into a JS string literal without escaping; a Referer containing a quote would break out of the string (minor, since the value is also attacker-controlled, but it is a JS injection point).

findings.title: URL scheme validation regex is over-permissive and inconsistent
findings.body: `return unless url =~ /^https?\:\/\//` — the escaped colons (`\:`) in a regex are just literal colons, so this works, but the pattern is not anchored at the end and accepts strings like `http://` followed by anything, including `http://evil.com" onmouseover=...` (relevant given the XSS in the same method) and `https:///path`. More importantly, the same check is duplicated (with slightly different escaping) in Jobs::PollFeed line 33 (`url !~ /^https?\:\/\//`) and TopicRetriever relies on URI parsing instead. There is no shared URL validator, so the three call sites can disagree about what is a valid embed URL. A single strict validator (scheme http/https, parseable URI, present host) should be used everywhere.

findings.title: import mutates the caller's contents string in place
findings.body: `contents << "\n<hr>\n..."` appends to the String passed in by the caller. In Jobs::PollFeed, `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` is a fresh string so it is mostly harmless there, but in TopicEmbed.import_remote, `doc.content` (the Readability document's content) is passed directly and gets the footer appended to it; any reuse of that string afterwards sees the mutated value. More subtly, the `content_sha1` is computed AFTER the mutation (line 16), which is correct for change detection, but the in-place mutation of an argument is a hidden side effect that violates the method's contract and will surprise callers (e.g. the disqus.thor importer or tests that reuse `contents`). Use `contents = contents + ...` or `<<` on a dup.

findings.title: Content-hash comparison uses the mutated string but the update path can silently skip revisions
findings.body: On update, `if content_sha1 != embed.content_sha1` triggers a PostRevisor revision. But `content_sha1` is computed from `contents` AFTER the 'imported from' footer was appended (line 13), while the stored hash was computed the same way on insert, so far so good. However, if the remote article's URL changes (e.g. trailing slash differences, http→https, redirects), a NEW TopicEmbed row is created for what is the same article, producing a duplicate topic — there is no canonicalization of `embed_url` (the unique index on embed_url then also silently allows near-duplicate URLs). Conversely, if only the footer link text changed, every row would be revised. The embed_url should be canonicalized (normalized URI: lowercase host, strip fragment, default ports, trailing slash) before lookup/insert.

findings.title: Feed polling fetches an admin-configured URL with open-uri without scheme/SSRF restrictions
findings.body: `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` uses Kernel#open on a URL. While the setting is admin-controlled, `open` on a string starting with `|` executes a shell command (the classic open-uri/Kernel#open pipe vulnerability) — if the setting value ever begins with `|` (or is otherwise attacker-influenced via a compromised admin UI, import, or YAML injection), this is remote command execution. Even restricting to http(s), there is no protection against SSRF to internal addresses (169.254.169.254, localhost services). The code should use `URI.parse` + `Net::HTTP`/`open-uri`'s `URI.open` equivalent with an explicit scheme whitelist (http/https only) and ideally block private/link-local IP ranges.

findings.title: import_remote fetches arbitrary URLs server-side (SSRF) with no scheme or host restrictions
findings.body: `Readability::Document.new(open(url).read, ...)` fetches `url` server-side. `url` originates from the `embed_url` request parameter (EmbedController#best → Jobs::RetrieveTopic → TopicRetriever → import_remote) and from RSS item links in PollFeed. TopicRetriever#invalid_host? restricts the host to `SiteSetting.embeddable_host`, but: (1) that check is bypassable — see the controller finding — and PollFeed passes `i.link`/`i.id` from the feed with only a `^https?://` regex check, so a malicious feed can make the server fetch `http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/` or internal services; (2) `open` has the pipe-command issue noted above. The fetch must be restricted to http/https and the resolved IP must be validated against private ranges, and the embeddable_host check must actually be enforced on this path.

findings.title: i.content can be nil, causing NoMethodError on .scrub
findings.body: `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` — SimpleRSS items do not guarantee a `content` element (it is optional in RSS 2.0; `content:encoded` may be absent, and Atom entries may only have `summary`). When absent, `i.content` is nil and `.scrub` raises NoMethodError, aborting the whole hourly poll (and since `sidekiq_options retry: false`, the failure is silent until someone notices missing imports). Guard with `i.content.to_s.scrub` or skip items without content.

findings.title: feed_key is defined but never used — Last-Modified/ETag caching is dead code
findings.body: `feed_key` builds a Redis key `"feed-modified:<sha1 of url>"` but nothing in the job ever reads or writes it. The apparent intent (per the key name) was to send a conditional GET (If-Modified-Since / If-None-Match) and skip re-parsing unchanged feeds, but `open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` is unconditional. Every hour the full feed is downloaded and every item is re-imported (TopicEmbed.import does dedupe by content hash, so no duplicate topics, but the work is wasted). Either implement the conditional fetch using feed_key or remove the dead method.

findings.title: invalid_host? treats a blank embeddable_host as matching any host
findings.body: `SiteSetting.embeddable_host != URI(@embed_url).host` — when `embeddable_host` is blank/nil (the default in config/site_settings.yml is `''`), `nil != "eviltrout.com"` is true, so invalid_host? returns true and retrieval is blocked. That part is fine. But the check is an exact host string comparison with no normalization: `http://EvilTrout.com/...` (case), `http://eviltrout.com:80/...` (explicit default port — URI#host drops the port so this actually matches), or `http://eviltrout.com./...` (trailing dot, which DNS resolves to the same host) will mismatch or match inconsistently. Host comparison must be done on the normalized, downcased host (and the same normalization must be applied in EmbedController's referer check and in TopicEmbed URL canonicalization), otherwise the allowlist is both bypassable (trailing-dot / case tricks against some resolvers) and brittle.

findings.title: RetrieveTopic triggers a full synchronous PollFeed run inside the request job
findings.body: perform_retrieve calls `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` inline when `feed_polling_enabled?`. PollFeed downloads and parses the entire RSS feed and imports every item (each import creates/revises posts). This runs inside the RetrieveTopic Sidekiq job, so a single embed request for a URL not yet in the feed can trigger a full feed crawl and bulk import — potentially minutes of work and dozens of post creations — while the user's embed request is waiting (the controller already rendered 'loading', but the job is blocked and Sidekiq workers are consumed). Worse, every distinct embed_url hit within the throttle window can re-trigger this. The poll should be enqueued as its own job (`Jobs.enqueue(:poll_feed)`) rather than executed inline, and the per-URL retrieval should not depend on a full feed scan.

findings.title: RetrieveTopic job is enqueued on every cache-miss request with no deduplication
findings.body: When no TopicEmbed exists for the URL, the controller enqueues `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)` and renders 'loading'. The loading page reloads every 30 seconds (app/views/embed/loading.html.erb), and each reload enqueues ANOTHER RetrieveTopic job. TopicRetriever has a 60-second Redis throttle (`retrieved_recently?`) that mitigates duplicate work, but: (1) the throttle key is per-URL and setnx-based, so the first job sets it and subsequent jobs bail — OK — but the throttle only lasts 60s while the loading page reloads every 30s indefinitely, so after 60s a new job is enqueued and the cycle repeats for as long as the topic is missing (e.g. the remote page is down or the import keeps failing), hammering the remote site and the job queue; (2) many concurrent viewers of the same not-yet-imported URL each enqueue jobs. There should be a longer-lived 'import in progress / failed' marker (e.g. a Redis key with a TTL of minutes, or a DB flag) so the job is enqueued at most once per N minutes per URL.

findings.title: EmbedController renders a TopicView for any user (including anonymous) without checking topic access
findings.body: `@topic_view = TopicView.new(topic_id, current_user, {best: 5})` — TopicView is constructed with `current_user`, which is nil for anonymous requests (the embed iframe is loaded cross-origin from the embedding site, so no Discourse session cookie is sent). Whether TopicView enforces access for nil users depends on its internals, but the embed endpoint then renders `post.cooked` raw for every post returned. If the embedded topic is in a restricted category, is a private message, or is otherwise not publicly visible, its content is exposed to anyone who knows/guesses the embed_url — and embed_urls are the external article URLs, which are often public. The controller must verify the topic is publicly visible (e.g. `Guardian.new(nil).can_see?(topic)` / topic.category.read_restricted check) before building the view, and return 404 otherwise.

findings.title: post.user can be nil, causing NoMethodError when rendering an embed
findings.body: The view calls `post.user.small_avatar_url` and `post.user.username` unconditionally. Posts whose author has been deleted (user_id retained but user row gone, or anonymous/system posts) will raise NoMethodError on nil, breaking the whole embed render (500). Guard with `post.user.present?` or use the existing `post.user` serializer pattern (e.g. `BasicUserSerializer`) / `post.username` (Post#username delegates to user.username and would also fail, so an explicit nil check or `try` is needed).

findings.title: absolutize_urls only handles root-relative URLs and mishandles protocol-relative and default ports
findings.body: The method rewrites only `href`/`src` values starting with `/`. Protocol-relative URLs (`//cdn.example.com/x.png`) and scheme-relative paths (`images/foo.png`) are left as-is, so images/links break when the content is viewed on the Discourse origin. Also, the port logic `prefix << ":#{uri.port}" if uri.port != 80 && uri.port != 443` appends the port for https URLs on port 80 or http URLs on port 443 incorrectly (it checks the numeric port against both schemes' defaults regardless of the actual scheme), and `URI#port` returns the default port when none is specified, so `http://host:80` gets no port (fine) but `https://host:443` also gets none (fine) — the real bug is non-default ports on the 'wrong' scheme and the fact that `uri.port` for a URI without an explicit port returns 80/443, making the condition mostly moot. Use `uri.origin` (Ruby 2.x) or build the prefix from scheme+host+optional non-default port, and handle `//`-prefixed and relative URLs via `URI.join`.

findings.title: no_throttle is granted based on the requesting user's staff status, but the job runs asynchronously and the check is per-request
findings.body: `TopicRetriever.new(args[:embed_url], no_throttle: user.try(:staff?))` — the throttle bypass is decided by whichever user happened to trigger the embed request. A staff member viewing the embed page bypasses the 60s throttle, so a staff user (or anyone who can get a staff account to load the page) can force repeated retrievals of the same URL, each performing an outbound HTTP fetch to the embeddable host (a self-DoS / amplification vector against the configured host). The throttle should be keyed on the URL only (as it is), and the staff bypass should either not exist or be rate-limited separately; at minimum the bypass should not be derived from an untrusted request parameter path.

findings.title: Controller spec expects TopicRetriever to be used synchronously, but the controller enqueues a job
findings.body: The test 'tells the topic retriever to work when no previous embed is found' stubs `TopicRetriever.expects(:new).returns(retriever)` and expects `retrieve` to be called during `get :best`. But the controller (app/controllers/embed_controller.rb line 15) calls `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)` — it never instantiates TopicRetriever in the request. In test mode `queue_jobs` is false (config/site_settings.yml developer.queue_jobs test: false), which may execute the job inline, but the spec does not stub Jobs.enqueue and does not assert on the enqueued job; if the job runs inline the mock expectation may pass by accident, and if jobs are queued the expectation fails. The spec should assert `Jobs.expects(:enqueue).with(:retrieve_topic, ...)` instead of mocking TopicRetriever, otherwise it is testing an implementation the controller does not have and will break or silently mislead.

findings.title: Update-path test does not verify the stored content_sha1 is updated, and update is not isolated from creation
findings.body: The 'Supports updating the post' test calls `TopicEmbed.import(user, url, title, "muhahaha new contents!")` and only asserts `post.cooked =~ /new contents/`. It does not verify that `embed.content_sha1` was updated (line 37 of the model uses `update_column`, which skips validations/callbacks — a regression there would go unnoticed), does not verify no second TopicEmbed row was created (the unique index would raise, but the test would surface it only as an error, not an assertion), and because the `let!(:post)` creation runs first, the test depends on ordering. A follow-up import with the SAME content should also be tested to confirm no revision occurs (the `content_sha1 != embed.content_sha1` guard).

findings.title: Spec requires the wrong job file and never tests poll_feed itself
findings.body: `require_dependency 'jobs/regular/process_post'` is unrelated to Jobs::PollFeed (which lives in app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb) — likely a copy-paste. More importantly, the spec only tests the `execute` guard conditions; `poll_feed` (the actual feed parsing, item URL fallback, content scrubbing, and TopicEmbed.import call) has no coverage at all, including the nil `i.content` crash and the URL fallback logic (`url = i.id if url.blank? || url !~ /^https?\:\/\//`). Add specs with a stubbed SimpleRSS feed covering: item with link, item with only id, item with no content, and verification that TopicEmbed.import is called with the right arguments.

findings.title: topic_embeds migration uses force: true, which drops an existing table
findings.body: `create_table :topic_embeds, force: true` — `force: true` drops the table if it already exists. In a migration this is dangerous: on any environment where the table was already created (e.g. by a previous partial run, a restored backup, or a plugin), running this migration silently destroys all topic_embeds rows (the mapping between external URLs and topics), after which every embed re-imports content as new topics. Migrations should use `create_table :topic_embeds` without force (the same applies to the unrelated change in 20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb, which also switched to `force: true`).

findings.title: cook_method raw_html bypasses sanitization for any post that sets it, with no guard on who can set it
findings.body: Post#cook returns `raw` verbatim when `cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, and PostCreator (lib/post_creator.rb line 216) copies `@opts[:cook_method]` onto the post whenever present. There is no validation restricting `raw_html` to trusted callers (e.g. staff or the embed importer): any code path that passes user-controlled `raw` together with `cook_method: raw_html` (or any future caller that forwards a request param into opts) stores and renders unsanitized HTML. The `cook_method` option should be stripped from user-facing PostCreator invocations (whitelist it to internal importers only), and ideally raw_html posts should still pass through Sanitize with a strict whitelist before being stored in `cooked`.

findings.title: Embed view renders post.cooked with raw, relying entirely on the cooking pipeline for safety
findings.body:
`
<%= raw post.cooked %>
` renders cooked HTML unescaped. This is consistent with the main forum, but combined with the raw_html cook method (see the TopicEmbed findings) it means imported feed content is rendered with zero sanitization in this iframe, which is embedded on third-party sites. The embed surface should be treated as higher risk: at minimum, posts shown here should be re-sanitized on output, and raw_html posts should never be displayed without a Sanitize pass.

findings.title: Embed route is defined before the /t/:id routes and lacks a format constraint
findings.body: `get 'embed/best' => 'embed#best'` is placed in the middle of the routes (line 245), before the topic routes. It does not conflict with existing routes, but it also has no `format: false` / constraints, so `/embed/best.json` or `/embed/best.xml` would match and run the controller (params[:embed_url] required, so it would 400 — minor). More relevant: the route is not constrained to GET-only semantics beyond the verb, and there is no rate limiting at the routing layer; combined with the per-request job enqueue finding, this endpoint is an easy amplification target. Consider `get 'embed/best' => 'embed#best', format: false` and Rack::Attack throttling on /embed/.

findings.title: discourse_expires_in is called even when rendering 'loading', caching a page that tells the client to reload
findings.body: `discourse_expires_in 1.minute` runs unconditionally at the end of `best`, including when the 'loading' template is rendered (line 16). The loading page contains a script that reloads after 30 seconds; caching it for 1 minute via the browser/CDN means a user whose import completes 5 seconds later still sees the cached loading page and waits for the reload. The loading response should be marked no-cache (or a very short expiry), while the successful embed view can be cached for 1 minute.

findings.title: Disqus importer now depends on TopicEmbed.import_remote fetching t[:link], but never passes created_at and loses the permalink post
findings.body: The refactored import calls `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])` and no longer creates the original permalink post (`raw: "[[Permalink](#{t[:link]})]"` with `created_at: Date.parse(t[:created_at])` was removed). Consequences: (1) the topic's created_at is now the import time, not the original thread creation date — topic ordering and 'new' lists are wrong for all imported threads; (2) the explicit permalink back to the Disqus thread is gone (import_remote's Readability extraction may or may not include it); (3) `import_remote` ignores any created_at option — TopicEmbed.import has no created_at parameter at all, so there is no way to preserve dates. The importer should pass `created_at` through TopicEmbed.import (add an opts parameter forwarded to PostCreator, which already supports `created_at`).

findings.title: Disqus importer creates users with User.create! which can raise and abort the whole import
findings.body: `post_user = User.create!(email: email, username: UserNameSuggester.suggest(email))` — the bang version raises on validation failure (duplicate email race, invalid username suggestion, etc.), and the exception is not rescued inside the `parser.threads.each` loop, so one bad author email aborts the entire import mid-way (the `ensure` restores settings but all remaining threads are lost, and already-created topics remain — a partial import with no idempotency). Use `User.create` and skip/fallback to the default user on failure, or rescue and log per-post.

findings.title: embed_by_username lookup will NoMethodError on nil if the setting is blank
findings.body: `User.where(username_lower: SiteSetting.embed_by_username.downcase)` — `execute` guards with `SiteSetting.embed_by_username.present?`, but `poll_feed` is a public method also invoked directly from TopicRetriever (lib/topic_retriever.rb line 41: `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` — that goes through execute, so guarded). However `feed_key` and `poll_feed` are public and the guard lives only in `execute`; any direct call to `poll_feed` (or a future refactor moving the guard) with a blank setting raises NoMethodError on nil.downcase. Move the blank check into poll_feed or use `SiteSetting.embed_by_username.to_s.downcase`.

findings.title: PostRevisor revision of an imported post does not preserve cook_method, so the update is re-cooked as Markdown
findings.body: On update, `PostRevisor.new(post).revise!(user, absolutize_urls(url, contents), skip_validations: true, bypass_rate_limiter: true)` sets a new `raw` (HTML). PostRevisor#update_post assigns `@post.raw = @new_raw` and saves; the Post `before_save` callback (app/models/post.rb line 321) recomputes `self.cooked = cook(raw, ...)` unless new_record?. `cook` checks `cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` — the post retains cook_method raw_html from creation, so cooked == raw. OK in the current flow. BUT: PostRevisor never touches cook_method, and if the post's cook_method were ever reset (e.g. by an edit through the normal UI, which doesn't set cook_method but also doesn't clear it — actually it persists), the HTML raw would be run through the Markdown pipeline and mangled. More importantly, the revision path relies on the column persisting; there is no test pinning that an updated imported post still has cook_method raw_html and cooked == raw. The spec gap is noted in the topic_embed_spec finding; additionally, `update_column(:content_sha1, ...)` skips callbacks — acceptable here, but if the revise! fails (returns false because raw unchanged — impossible here since contents changed) the hash would still be updated, desyncing hash from content. Guard: only update the hash if the revision actually happened.

findings.title: Script assumes #discourse-comments exists; throws if the host page lacks it
findings.body: `document.getElementById('discourse-comments')` returns null if the embedding page does not include the expected div, and `comments.appendChild(iframe)` then throws TypeError, leaving a broken embed. The embed snippet should be documented to require the div, and the script should fail gracefully (or create the container) when it is missing.

findings.title: postMessage resize only fires on window.onload and never on content changes
findings.body: The iframe height is sent once on `window.onload`. If the embed content grows after load (images loading, fonts, the loading→content transition when the topic finishes importing and the page reloads — that case is covered by reload, but late-loading avatars/images in best.html.erb are not), the iframe keeps its initial height and content is clipped (scrolling is disabled via `iframe.scrolling = "no"` in embed.js). A ResizeObserver or periodic height check should be used, or at minimum re-send after images load.

findings.title: cook_method default of 1 assumes Enum ordering that is not enforced at the DB level
findings.body: `add_column :posts, :cook_method, :integer, default: 1, null: false` — the default 1 is meant to be `Post.cook_methods[:regular]` (Enum.new(:regular, :raw_html) → regular=1? Discourse's Enum typically starts at 1, so regular=1, raw_html=2). This is correct only if Enum assigns 1 to the first key; the migration hardcodes 1 with no comment or check constraint, so if the Enum definition is reordered, existing rows silently point at the wrong method. Add a comment documenting the mapping, or better, verify in a data migration that the value matches Post.cook_methods[:regular].

findings.title: TopicRetriever spec never tests perform_retrieve, fetch_http, or the Redis throttle
findings.body: All specs stub out `perform_retrieve` or `retrieved_recently?`; the actual retrieval logic (the exists? check, the PollFeed delegation, fetch_http user lookup and import_remote call) and the `retrieved_recently?` Redis setnx/expire logic are completely untested. The throttle is security-relevant (prevents hammering the remote host), so a regression that removes the expire or inverts the setnx result would go unnoticed. Add specs using mock_redis (already a test dependency) for retrieved_recently?, and stub TopicEmbed.import_remote / Jobs::PollFeed for perform_retrieve/fetch_http.
